summary:
Commit c446f4d33 on top of fe4133cf2. The run branch at fe4133cf2 had only dyna-admin, dyna-ci, dyna-discord and dyna-workflows merged. dyna-diagnose, dyna-services and the rewritten dyna-nodes, dyna-images and dyna-extend were still on their own fix branches, so I brought in each one's final version (a56646a7, 5a0911b6, ab721aa0, 752169bf, cce0f9a5) and merged their skills_test.go expectations by hand.
1. Descriptions: I rewrote all ten as one list. Each starts "Use when", and together they come to about 1,580 characters. The splits: CI runs that look stuck go to dyna-ci, not dyna-diagnose. More or other machines (pool-node/pool-failed, adding a host, pool or GPU machine) go to dyna-nodes. Other stuck sessions, boxes and full hosts go to dyna-diagnose. Settings and decisions go to dyna-admin, and add-ons to dyna-extend. Contents lists are gone from dyna-workflows and dyna-discord.
2. One place per fact:
- How to run the owner CLI on the engine host is stated in dyna-admin. dyna-nodes, dyna-diagnose, dyna-services and dyna-extend now say "owner CLI (dyna-admin)" in one line.
- Reading and recording a room's host rule lives in dyna-admin, and dyna-nodes points to it.
- dyna-extend owns addon set: dyna-admin's add-on paragraph is now a table row pointing there.
- Who decides global add-ons lives in dyna-admin. dyna-extend points to it.
- Box sizes, memory and disk live in the table in dyna-images. dyna-nodes and dyna-workflows point to it.
- Host removal with --discard-boxes lives in dyna-nodes. dyna-diagnose points to it.
- Waiting on box capacity is in dyna-diagnose. dyna-nodes keeps only the pool reasons and adds pointers back.
- In dyna-images, the box-needs host restriction now points to dyna-admin, not dyna-nodes.
Every cross-reference names one of the ten skills that exist.
3. dyna-local-proxy: added `dyna-audience: root` and a description starting "Root only."; nothing else changed. dyna-admin, dyna-diagnose, dyna-nodes, dyna-services and dyna-local-proxy carry the line, and the other five do not. A new test, TestRootOnlySkills, enforces this, plus each description under 300 characters and the descriptions together under 1,700.
4. Terms and openings:
- Skills are named bare ("dyna-admin", not "skill dyna-admin" or "the dyna-admin skill"), and every H1 names a task, e.g. "Diagnose sessions, boxes and hosts", "Add machines: hosts and node pools", "Answer and act on Discord", "Write and run Dyna workflows".
- "Engine host named in your prompt", "owner CLI", "root" and "parent" are used the same way throughout.
5. go test ./box/skills passes. Expectations updated: dyna-extend, dyna-nodes and dyna-ci descriptions, and the nodes and extend phrase lists. Added the dyna-images, dyna-diagnose and dyna-services phrase tests. BuiltIn now counts 10 skills.
unverified: next/engine/addon_box_test.go (TestAddonsInARealBox, line 281) still expects dyna-extend's old description "Use when you need to add a skill or mcp server to dyna". It skipped here (no real box available), but it will fail wherever it actually runs. The fix is outside next/box/skills, so I left it: change it to the new description.

I did not run every command in the merged-in skills (diagnose, services, nodes, images, extend) against `--help` again; their own writer and fix steps checked them. `dyna addon`, `account` and `session set-account` are not in this tree's CLI (they are in the parallel code PR), and the frontmatter key dyna-audience has no effect until that PR lands.
dyna-local-proxy's example model name claude-opus-5-5 and its failure table were left as they were and not re-checked against a live proxy.
Some table rows run past 100 characters, up to about 280 in dyna-local-proxy, which I left unchanged.
